 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr.Arvind Kumar, Advocate  For the Opposite Party/s : Mr.Ram Sumiran Rai, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE CHANDRA SHEKHAR JHA

ORAL ORDER 4 26-02-2026 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners and learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the State.
2. The accused/petitioners apprehending their arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 923 of 2016 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 417, 420 of the IPC.
3.

As per complaint, petitioners alleged to establish physical relation for couple of days with complainant on false pretext of marriage and, thereafter, fraudulently taken her money total of Rs. 3 lacs.
With aforesaid allegation, the complaint was filed for the offence punishable under Sections 376/417/420 Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.80226 of 2025(4) dt.26-02-2026 of the Indian Penal Code..

4. It is submitted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners that the main allegation as to commit rape on false pretext of marriage was not believed by learned trial court during enquiry and, therefore, the cognizance was not taken for the offence alleged under Section 376 of the IPC.

It is submitted that the learned trial court took cognizance only for the offence punishable under Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47735592/
1 Sections 417 and 420 of the IPC, which was primarily taken believing the statement of complainant that she advanced loan of Rs. 3 lacs to the petitioners.

sentences.text: It is submitted that in view of same, the dispute appears primarily civil in nature.

5. Arguing further, it is submitted that complaint in issue also not appears supported by affidavit and, therefore, the allegation as raised through FIR also not appears legally sustainable in view of legal report of Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through Priyanka Srivastava Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh [2015 (6) SCC 287].
6.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh [2015 (6) SCC 287]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned APP, duly assisted by learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant, while opposing the prayer of bail submitted that after Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.80226 of 2025(4)
dt.26-02-2026 withdrawal of cash of Rs. 3 lacs from the bank, the amount in issue was paid to petitioners.

7. In view of aforesaid factual submissions and by taking note of fact as primarily dispute between the parties appears civil in nature, where the allegation of rape on false pretext of marriage was not believed by the learned jurisdictional magistrate, accordingly, both above named petitioners, in the event of their arrest or surrender before the learned trial Court, within a period of four weeks of the order, is directed to be released on bail furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand)
each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gaya/concerned Court, where the case is pending in connection with Complaint Case No. 923 of 2016 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the BNSS.

(Chandra Shekhar Jha, J) veena/-
